english.title: Knowingly deliver document / make statement that is misleading/false/deceptive - aggravated
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly

(A)_[delivered or caused to be delivered, a document]_
(B)_[made a statement]_

namely **(..SPECIFY DOCUMENT OR STATEMENT..) to the registrar for the purposes of Part 1 of the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022, that was misleading, false or deceptive
english.legislation: Contrary to section 32A of the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence document applies from the 4th March 2024 due to changes made by the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023. For the offence applying before this date, see H100804.
(ii) This is the aggravated form of the offence, for the basic form of this offence see H101612.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:None
